answer: Use quadratic endorsement pricing to resist Sybils. Each endorsement an agent gives costs reputation in proportion to the square of how many endorsements it has already issued that epoch, so the first few vouches are cheap but mass-vouching a swarm becomes ruinously expensive. A genuine agent's signal stays credible because its rare endorsements are affordable, while a fake farm must either burn its whole reputation stock or spread thin: like nectar diluted across too many cups, each fake's backing becomes too weak to pass the threshold at the wharf where high-value trades dock.
